tier_reason: Stays A (csv-parser benchmarks/README.md, public harness). Enricher caveat corrections: AVX2 asymmetry in the harness and start-up-dominated 500K rows; float parser not correctly rounded.

corrections.caveats: Third-party competitor harness (vincentlaucsb/csv-parser benchmarks/README.md, 'CMake Release', unpinned master): wins only the 500K and 5M clean-read rows and loses 5M count, 5M quoted read, materialization and 4+ worker reads; the csv-parser targets get /arch:AVX2 through a PUBLIC compile option while the standalone fast-cpp binary gets no AVX2, and the result JSON shows the 500K wins mostly measure csv-parser start-up cost (csv-parser count 196 MB/s at 500K vs 543 MB/s at 5M, fast-cpp flat at 315-350 MB/s). Harnesses differ (fast-cpp copies all 8 fields). Correctness: the float parser is not correctly rounded (issue #122), empty numeric cells silently become 0, the real line limit is 2^20 (block_len) not 2^24-1, and the default reader has no quote handling. Last commit 2025-02-02.

tier_reason: Stays B (cmark benchmarks.md, independent). Enricher caveat corrections: sdbm-hash-only reference-link matching, REF_TABLE_SIZE 8, max_nesting drop, dialect mismatch.

corrections.caveats: cmark benchmarks.md (tags 0.21.0-0.29.0): hoedown 0.21 s vs cmark 0.29 s vs discount 1.85 s on an 11 MB Pro Git input, Core 2 Duo 2 GHz, public make bench, no compiler or flags; the bench ran hoedown's CLI defaults (no extensions), a different dialect from cmark, and the row was dropped at cmark 0.30.0. Pathological input takes 17.84 s. Correctness: reference links are matched by a 32-bit sdbm hash only (link_ref stores no label), so colliding labels resolve to the wrong URL; REF_TABLE_SIZE 8 makes 160,000 references take 8.78 s (issue #223); content nested past max_nesting 16 is silently dropped; no javascript: scheme filtering. Abandoned since 2015-12-07.

tier_reason: Stays C (author's 1988 comp.compilers table, snippet only, no harness). Enricher corrections: licence SPDX tag and fuller caveats.

corrections.caveats: Evidence is Paxson's 1988 comp.compilers post 88-04-001 (repeated as 'old timings' in 90-11-063), seen only as a search snippet since compilers.iecc.com is blocked: lex 29.8 s vs flex 19.3/9.0/7.8 s run time (flex -cf 3.8x), with a 126.5K vs 41.0K object and scanner generation 83.0 s (lex) vs 3.9 s; no harness code, author's own numbers, the repo has no lex timings. The fastest -CF mode has an open ASan global-buffer-overflow (#628, since Feb 2024) and -Cf/-CF default to 7-bit tables that often hang or crash on 8-bit input; generation blowup #326 (45 s), 32000 NFA-state cap #572. Last release 2.6.4 (May 2017) while master documents unreleased --emit backends; CVE-2016-6354 in scanners generated by 2.5.36-2.6.0; byte-only, no Unicode.

tier_reason: Stays C (first-party). Enricher caveat correction: 2013 numbers from a zero-copy, pre-read UCL run against an unpublished jansson build.

corrections.caveats: First-party README numbers (parse 0.6649 s vs jansson 1.3899 s) unchanged since tag 0.2.0 (2013-12-03), before the uthash-to-klib switch in 0.7.0; one run each, mixed -O levels, JSON-only evidence. test_speed.c starts the timer after mmap and parses ZEROCOPY while speed.test pre-reads the file ('Preread file to cheat benchmark!'); the jansson harness, version and flags were never published. Workload is public: tests/rcl_test.json.xz (19,001,364 bytes, 693,050 lines), best figure about 63 MB/s (-O3, derived). Many open fuzzer-found memory-safety issues (#352 ZEROCOPY use-after-free with add_file, #388, #387, #367); the hash seed defaults to time(NULL) through an unsynchronized static.
